One day in the life of 6,146 Americans

atus_days.Rd

How each respondent to the 2025 American Time Use Survey (ATUS) spent the 24 hours of their diary day, collapsed into 15 everyday activity categories, together with a few characteristics of the respondent and the day type the day was assigned to.

Usage

atus_days

Format

A tibble with 6,146 rows and 25 columns:

id

ATUS case identifier (TUCASEID).

weight

ATUS final survey weight (TUFINLWGT).

age

Age in years (TEAGE; 80 to 84 recorded as 80, 85 and over as 85).

sex

Sex, "Male" or "Female" (TESEX).

employed

Is the respondent employed (TELFS 1 or 2)?

student

Is the respondent enrolled in high school, college or university (TESCHENR)? Only asked of people aged 15 to 49; others are FALSE.

youngest_child_age

Age of the youngest own child under 18 in the household (TRYHHCHILD); NA if none.

weekend

Was the diary day a Saturday or Sunday?

sleep, personal_care, eating, work, education, housework, childcare, adult_care, shopping_services, socialising, screen, other_leisure, exercise, religious_volunteer, travel

Minutes spent in each activity category; see activity_categories.

other

Minutes that could not be coded (ATUS codes 50xxxx).

day_type

Day type the day was assigned to; see day_types.

The 15 activity columns plus other add up to 1,440 minutes for every row.

Source

U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, American Time Use Survey 2025, Activity Summary file, https://www.bls.gov/tus/data/datafiles-2025.htm. BLS data are in the public domain. Prepared in data-raw/atus_days.R.

Details

Each row is one person's diary for one day (4am to 4am), so a "day type" describes a day, not a person. Weekends are over-sampled in the ATUS: use weight for any estimate about the population.
